title: A comparative evaluation of LSC and LSCF cathodes for low-temperature solid oxide fuel cells
content: Lanthanum-based perovskite oxides have been extensively investigated as cathode materials for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), particularly for low- and intermediate-temperature operation, due to their high catalytic activity, reduced polarization and tunable oxygen vacancy concentration. In this study, La0.5Sr0.5CoO3 (LSC) and La0.6Sr0.4Co0.2Fe0.8O3 (LSCF) cathode materials were synthesized via a sol–gel approach, thus controlling homogeneity, enhancing surface area and improving cation dispersion. The synthesized materials were further calcined to obtain pure perovskite structures, followed by the fabrication of symmetrical cells using samarium-doped ceria (SDC) as an electrolyte to evaluate the electrochemical performance at different operating temperatures. Structural and morphological analyses revealed relatively uniform particle distributions and porous cathode morphologies, which are favorable for gas diffusion and enhance the ORR kinetics. The open-circuit voltages (OCVs) of the fabricated cells remained stable across the tested temperature range. The variations in OCVs with operating temperature reflect the electrochemical behavior of the fabricated cells under the investigated testing conditions. Electrochemical testing demonstrated the measurable electrochemical activity of both LSC and LSCF cathodes at reduced operating temperatures, with LSCF showing higher power output than LSC under the investigated conditions. The maximum power densities for LSC and LSCF were 395 and 541 mW cm−2 at 450 °C, 536 and 615 mW cm−2 at 500 °C, 639 and 684 mW cm−2 at 550 °C, and 680 and 791 mW cm−2 at 600 °C, respectively. The maximum power densities for LSC and LSCF of 395 mW cm−2 and 541 mW cm−2 at 450 °C, respectively, show the strong ORR activity and improved electrolyte–cathode compatibility at lower temperature. Overall, the superior electrochemical performance of LSCF compared with LSC under the investigated conditions highlights the potential of the LSCF composition as a promising cathode material for reduced-temperature SOFC applications.
